MLS listing classification uses the name "Burnaby Lake" differently: as a Burnaby South band around Canada Way and Rosewood Street, south of Highway 1 by Deer Lake and Robert Burnaby Park, where the current "Burnaby Lake" listings are detached houses, not condos.
Streets, schools and getting around Burnaby Lake

items.t: The sub-area wraps Burnaby Lake Regional Park. The lake and park themselves are not residential land: the park is a Metro Vancouver regional park of 360 acres, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978, with a 25-year City/Metro Vancouver lease signed. No condo can front the lake because the shoreline is parkland.

West and north-west side: the Sperling and Kensington streets below Lougheed Highway. East side: Government Road and Beaverbrook, toward Lougheed Town Centre. Lougheed Highway is the northern anchor road.
Recreation anchors: the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex and the Bill Copeland Sports Centre at 3676 Kensington Avenue (2,000 seats).
Transit anchor: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station, served by routes 110, 134 and 144.
Schools beside the edges: Sperling Elementary (2200 Sperling Avenue), École Seaforth (7881 Government Road) and Burnaby Central Secondary (6011 Deer Lake Parkway).
Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere verified —. The residential streets in both the park-wrap geography and the MLS-named southern band are detached-house streets.

The arena beside the lake seats 2,000. The Bill Copeland Sports Centre at 3676 Kensington Avenue, part of the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex, is a 2,000-seat facility — event-night traffic on Kensington Avenue is a real factor for the streets west of the park.

Streets, schools and getting around Burnaby Lake

items.t: "Burnaby Lake" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby; the sub-area wraps Burnaby Lake Regional Park in central-east Burnaby — the residential streets on the lake's edges (the Sperling and Kensington side to the west and north-west, the Government Road and Beaverbrook side to the east) around a large regional park and lake that are not themselves residential land.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: in the park-wrap geography, nowhere verified — the residential streets are detached-house streets.

Park and recreation anchors: Burnaby Lake Regional Park is a 360-acre Metro Vancouver regional park, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978 under a 25-year City/Metro Vancouver lease; the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex (5 lit artificial turf fields, 17 tennis courts in the City's listings) and the Bill Copeland Sports Centre, 3676 Kensington Avenue (2,000 seats), sit at the Kensington/Sperling side.

Transit anchor: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway, at the sub-area's north-west side — you can walk into the park directly from the station — with bus routes 110, 134 and 144 connecting there.

Schools beside the edges: School District 41 (Burnaby) runs 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools with no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12), and catchments are address-based through the SD41 locator. Schools on the Province's list beside the sub-area include Sperling Elementary (K–7), 2200 Sperling Ave, École Seaforth Elementary (K–7), 7881 Government Rd, and Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway; no SD41 school sits on the park lands.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Burnaby Lake

items.t: Lake-edge checks: the lake shore is low, marshy protected wildlife habitat — Metro Vancouver's park materials describe the shoreline habitat the trails and boardwalks are built around — so lake-edge and creek-edge lots need parcel-level flood, habitat and watercourse-setback checks; a floodplain designation for the sub-area's residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read.

Burnaby property taxes and utilities: 2026 property taxes were due Friday, July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty after the July due date and a further 5% penalty after the September due date; Council approved a 2.9% increase (about $61 on the average home). The 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use and a garbage toter fee; the detached single-family water charge is $652.33, with a 5% discount if paid by the due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Burnaby Lake

items.t: The park has been regionally run for almost five decades (researched Nov 1, 2026). Metro Vancouver has managed Burnaby Lake Regional Park since 1978, and the City and Metro Vancouver have signed a 25-year lease agreement securing that management, with a Park Management Plan to be developed with the City within five years — the greenbelt around the lake is a settled long-term arrangement, not land awaiting development.
The one townhome complex is marketed under a different lake's name (checked Nov 1, 2026).
A 33% sales ratio here means one sale (as of September 2026). Quoting the percentage without the counts misleads in both directions.

The arena beside the lake seats 2,000 (researched Nov 1, 2026). The Bill Copeland Sports Centre at 3676 Kensington Avenue, part of the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex, is a 2,000-seat venue (1,984 permanent seats) used for hockey, lacrosse, events and concerts — event-night traffic on Kensington Avenue is a real factor for the streets west of the park, and City programs there continue during construction of the new recreation complex.

The realistic future strata route here is SSMUH, not a project (researched Nov 1, 2026). Under Burnaby's Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) R1 rules, a house lot can hold 3 units (lots up to 280 m²), 4 units (larger lots) or 6 units (lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop), and multi-unit lots may be stratified — small strata product on these streets would arrive lot by lot, not as a named complex.
Jared's own sold history in this sub-area is not verified (researched Nov 1, 2026).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Burnaby Lake

items.t: Burnaby Lake is a City of Burnaby GVR board sub-area wrapping Burnaby Lake Regional Park in central-east Burnaby — residential streets on the lake's edges (Sperling/Kensington west and north-west, Government Road/Beaverbrook east) around a large regional park and lake that are not themselves residential land. Burnaby Lake Regional Park is a Metro Vancouver regional park; "Burnaby Lake" the sub-area is the housing around it.
Nearby areas: Montecito and Sperling-Duthie north and west, Government Road east, Burnaby Hospital and Deer Lake south-west, Lougheed Town Centre further east along Lougheed Highway.

Main roads: Lougheed Highway (north), Winston Street, Sperling Avenue, Kensington Avenue and Government Road; Highway 1 runs along the lake's south side. Transit: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway, walkable into the park, with bus routes 110, 134 and 144 connecting there; route 110 runs past the lake's north and west sides between Lougheed Station and Metrotown Station. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.
Nearest hospital: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, immediately south-west.

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) — 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide, no middle-school tier (K–7 / 8–12). SD41 schools beside the sub-area on the Province's list: Sperling Elementary (K–7), 2200 Sperling Ave; École Seaforth Elementary (K–7), 7881 Government Rd; Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Burnaby Lake

items.t: Lake-edge diligence: the lake shore is low, marshy wildlife habitat; a floodplain designation for the sub-area's residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read. For lake-edge and creek-edge lots, check flood, habitat and watercourse-setback conditions early — setback surprises surface late in deals.

Bare-land strata rules (applies to any bare-land strata lot, if one is ever verified here): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Burnaby Lake ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

blocks.text: Good to know about Burnaby Lake

items.t: The park's management is locked in for a generation (Feb 5, 2025): the City and Metro Vancouver signed a 25-year lease for Burnaby Lake Regional Park; Metro Vancouver continues to fund maintenance, natural resource protection, enforcement and capital improvements, and will develop a Park Management Plan with the City within five years — the green edge beside these lots is not a future development phase.

Two lakes' names are used interchangeably on Canada Way: Savile Row is filed under Burnaby Lake and marketed as the "heart of Deer Lake" — a buyer searching only one lake's name will miss or double-count product around the south edge.

The sports complex is the west side's real amenity engine: 5 lit artificial turf fields, 17 tennis courts in the City's listings, and the 2,000-seat Bill Copeland rink — with programs continuing during construction of the new recreation centre, so the amenity story carries a construction period with it.

faq.a: A buyer set on strata living here is looking at townhomes, or at the neighbouring sub-areas' stock.
faq.q: Are there any condos around Burnaby Lake at all?

faq.a: No. Burnaby Lake is a 360-acre Metro Vancouver regional park, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978 under a 25-year City/Metro lease; the shoreline is parkland, not residential lots. The closest housing is on the streets around the park.
faq.q: Can I buy a home right on the lake?

faq.a: One documented townhome complex: Savile Row at 5122–5152 Canada Way (built 2018, GBL Architects, freehold strata, 3 storeys) — filed by the MLS under Burnaby Lake even though its own marketing calls the location the "heart of Deer Lake."

Because MLS sub-area naming and the research geography genuinely differ: the board's "Burnaby Lake" band sits in Burnaby South (Canada Way / Rosewood Street, south of Highway 1), while the park-wrap geography uses Sperling/Kensington and Government Road/Beaverbrook. Search both usages or records get missed.
faq.q: Why do listings call the Canada Way / Rosewood streets "Burnaby Lake" when they're by Deer Lake?

faq.a: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station, with bus routes 110, 134 and 144 — the usable transit anchor for the park's west side; the Government Road side is served along the Lougheed corridor.
Both bases are stated in — a buyer searching only one lake's name will miss or double-count it.
faq.q: Is Savile Row really a Burnaby Lake complex?

faq.a: Strata: listings record freehold strata title, 3 storeys, built 2018, GBL Architects — so the Form B route applies in full, and its unit count and published restrictions are not confirmed until the strata documents are read.
faq.q: Strata or fee-simple at Savile Row?

faq.a: No. Burnaby Lake is a 360-acre Metro Vancouver regional park, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978 under a 25-year City/Metro lease; the shoreline is parkland, not residential lots. The closest housing is on the streets around the park.
faq.q: Can I buy a home right on the lake?
Is Burnaby Lake a neighbourhood or a park?
faq.a: Both names are in use for different things: Burnaby Lake Regional Park is a 360-acre Metro Vancouver regional park around the lake, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978 under a 25-year lease agreement with the City, and "Burnaby Lake" is also the GVR MLS® sub-area name for the housing on the streets around it.

faq.q: What can you do at Burnaby Lake?
faq.a: Metro Vancouver describes a wildlife sanctuary with walking trails, viewing towers and docks, a Nature House, and a rowing course with a pavilion and public canoe launch at the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex; the complex itself has 5 lit artificial turf fields and 17 tennis courts in the City's listings.

faq.q: How is transit at Burnaby Lake?
faq.a: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) sits at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway at the area's north-west side, you can walk into the park directly from the station, and buses 110, 134 and 144 connect there — the 144 links the station to Metrotown and SFU.
